answer: Anyone can insure an identity against clonehood at a market rate, and when the identity is proved to be a clone the insurer pays out of its own reserve, which turns detection into a revenue stream for whoever performs it. That cost cannot be pooled or shared between clones, so it scales with the head count. The nadir is the premium, the crystal the underwriting pool that pays on a clone proof, and the ember the correlated funding that sets the price; the nadir scales with the ember, and the crystal only pays when the clone is actually proved.
